Archive rates: our verified ESPNcricinfo ball-by-ball captures of men's T20 matches with line and length (1,632 back-of-a-length balls on the stumps in overs 17-20; 140 sixes, 32 straight, shot direction from Cricinfo's wagon zones 4 and 5) and Cricsheet men's T20 chases (25-31 needed off 8 balls, at most 5 down: 4 wins in 29, a small sample): analysis/kohli_rauf.py. 'In our archive': the archive is a sample, not the full history.

Quotes: Kohli, Star Sports interview, November 2023, as reported by PTI/Outlook India https://www.outlookindia.com/sports/icc-cricket-world-cup-2023-virat-kohli-focuses-on-learning-new-strokes-rather-than-becoming-a-complete-batter-news-330035 ; Rauf (Cricwick, December 2022) as reported by PTI/ThePrint https://theprint.in/sport/would-have-felt-hurt-if-pandya-or-dk-hit-me-for-sixes-but-kohli-is-different-class-haris-rauf/1243640 and DNA India https://www.dnaindia.com/cricket/report-don-t-think-he-can-do-that-again-haris-rauf-on-virat-kohli-s-straight-six-vs-pakistan-in-t20-world-cup-3015621 ; the shot's description (footwork, length, the flick) from SportsCafe https://sportscafe.in/blogs/untold-stories/what-was-kohli-thinking-during-those-monumental-sixes-against-haris-rauf . Reports differ on the length of the first six and on the direction of the second; the video says so.
The figure and the pitch map are our own illustrations, not a replay or the actual delivery. Photographs: supplied by the channel owner.

short.vo: Twenty-eight needed. Eight balls. हारिस रऊफ had given just twenty-two runs in three overs. In our archive, a chase like this works about one time in seven.

scene.title: 28 off 8.
scene.name: VIRAT KOHLI
scene.caption: Chasing 160 against Pakistan
scene.chip_sub: SUCH CHASES WON, IN OUR ARCHIVE (SMALL SAMPLE)

short.vo: India were four down. रऊफ, by his own account, had bowled three slower balls. A sensible person calls this a two-ball problem. विराट कोहली was not available for sensible.
Four balls, three runs. रऊफ was winning the over. Then two balls, twelve runs.

head.sub: RUNS OFF EACH BALL · HARIS RAUF

short.vo: The fifth ball, as most reports describe it: back of a length, on the stumps, at pace. In our archive, that ball at the death goes for six about one time in twelve. Straight, over the bowler's head: one in fifty-one.

head.sub: ILLUSTRATIVE · REPORTS DIFFER ON THE EXACT LENGTH

panels.title: BACK OF A LENGTH, ON THE STUMPS
stats: SUCH BALLS HIT FOR SIX AT THE DEATH

scene.footnote: IN OUR ARCHIVE OF MEN'S T20 CRICKET, OVERS 17 TO 20

short.vo: One: the boundaries at the MCG are long, say the reports. The ball has to clear the bowler first, then keep going.

scene.sub: The ball must clear the bowler first, then keep going.

short.vo: Two: a back-of-length ball at pace leaves the least time. You cannot start early. You decide, or you don't.

scene.sub: Back of a length, at pace: you decide, or you don't.

short.vo: Three: straight means over the bowler's head. A mistimed hit finds a fielder. A late decision finds the stumps.

scene.sub: Straight means over his head. Hit it late and it finds the stumps.

short.vo: Four: if it fails, India need twenty-eight off seven. If it works, sixteen off six. The archive does not do fear. It is just rude about the odds.

head.sub: THE SCOREBOARD AFTER THE FIFTH BALL

tiles.l: THE ARCHIVE'S ODDS FOR A STRAIGHT SIX

short.vo: So how? Reports say he moved across his stumps, made room, got back, and punched through the line with a straight bat. Not a slog. A drive that kept going up.

scene.note: Four phases drawn from the reports. Our own figure, not a replay.

short.vo: Asked later, विराट कोहली said: till this date, I don't know how I pulled off that shot. So we are in the same position.

scene.sub: “Till this date, I don't know how I pulled off that shot but it happened.”

short.vo: रऊफ said he had no idea कोहली could hit him down the ground off that length, and that he doesn't think he can do it again.

scene.sub: He had no idea Kohli could hit him down the ground off that length, and does not think he can do it again.

short.vo: The sixth ball, a flick. Reports disagree on whether it went behind square or over fine leg. Everyone agrees it went out.

scene.sub: Reports differ: behind square, or over fine leg.

short.vo: Then the last over. A no-ball, and a six. A wide. A free hit, कोहली bowled, three byes. A stumping, a wide, and a single off the last ball. Nobody's plan survived that over.
Eighty-two off fifty-three. Three of his four sixes came in the final eight balls. India won off the last ball.

scene.caption: Three of his four sixes came in the final eight balls
scene.chip_sub: SIXES IN THE LAST EIGHT BALLS

short.vo: So we checked the archive. One in fifty-one. Some call it the shot of the century. We call it a number that was never meant to apply to him.

scene.sub: Some call it the shot of the century. We call it a number that was never meant to apply to him.

short.vo: Which was the better six? Comment one, the straight one. Two, the flick. Three, the no-ball.

short.title: The Shot Kohli Can't Explain | India vs Pakistan T20 World Cup 2022 #Shorts
short.description:
India vs Pakistan, T20 World Cup 2022 at the MCG: Virat Kohli's two sixes off Haris Rauf in the 19th over, 28 needed off 8 balls. Why the straight six was so hard to play (in our archive, a back-of-a-length ball on the stumps at the death goes for six about 1 time in 12, and for a straight six about 1 in 51), how the reports say he played it, Kohli's and Rauf's own words, and the last over: a no-ball six, a free hit and three byes. Reports differ on some details of the delivery; we say where. Comment 1 the straight six, 2 the flick, 3 the no-ball six.
